anti_overlap: fd-pavement-survey-cadence: that agent focuses on interval spacing and detection error; this agent focuses on what statistic to compute once samples are collected
fd-hydro-survey-coverage: that agent focuses on spatial coverage gaps; this agent focuses on bias in the aggregation of valid samples
fd-mobile-airquality-calibration: that agent focuses on whether the raster is trustworthy; this agent assumes the raster is correct and critiques the aggregation math
decision_lens: Does the chosen aggregation (arithmetic proportion) minimize routing decision error, or does the distribution shape of sun/shade along an edge favor a different statistic?
distance_rationale: Precision agriculture practitioners fly transect lines over fields, extract per-pixel NDVI, and must collapse thousands of readings per parcel into a single actionable scalar (mean, median, percentile) that drives variable-rate application — the same aggregation problem as collapsing N shadow samples into one sun_fraction per edge.
expected_isomorphisms: The choice of mean vs. median vs. weighted percentile in NDVI aggregation has well-documented sensitivity to outliers and skewed distributions; a binary shadow raster (0/1) is maximally bimodal, so the brainstorm's arithmetic mean (in_sun / total) is equivalent to a proportion estimator — the NDVI literature's critique of mean-as-representative transfers directly to whether proportion is the right aggregation for routing.
focus: Aggregation method correctness and bias — whether arithmetic proportion is the right statistic for a binary raster feeding a multiplicative cost function
name: fd-agri-ndvi-aggregation
persona: Apply the perspective of a precision agriculture remote sensing analyst who aggregates drone NDVI imagery to per-management-zone prescriptions, selecting aggregation statistics that minimize decision error for variable-rate application.
review_areas: The felt-minute formula is multiplicative: time × (1 + 0.5 × sun_fraction). Arithmetic mean sun_fraction is unbiased for expected shade exposure on a homogeneous edge but is biased for routing decisions when shadow is clustered — a 50 m fully-shaded midblock segment and a uniformly dappled 50 m edge both yield sun_fraction=0.5 but have different comfort profiles

The brainstorm treats all samples as equal weight regardless of their position along the edge — NDVI practice distinguishes between simple mean and length-weighted mean; here all samples are equidistant so they are implicitly length-weighted, but this should be stated explicitly

The binary nature of the raster (0 or 1, no partial shade) means the proportion estimator is equivalent to a Bernoulli sample mean — the variance is p(1-p)/n, which is maximized at p=0.5. Edges near 50% sun_fraction have the highest estimation uncertainty yet receive no uncertainty flag

Whether a run-length encoding of the shadow profile (longest contiguous shade run as a fraction of edge length) would be a useful companion metric for human comfort vs. pure proportion — a long shade run enables sustained cooling, while alternating 5 m patches do not

The clip in the vectorized lookup silently maps out-of-bounds samples to boundary pixels — these fabricated values enter the numerator/denominator as legitimate observations, biasing sun_fraction for edges at the raster boundary

The nodata exclusion from both terms is correct for proportion estimation but has a subtle edge case: if a building occludes the DSM precisely over a consistently shaded canyon, the nodata may be correlated with shade, making the remaining sample set unrepresentative

severity_examples.example: The np.clip boundary guard silently replaces out-of-bounds sample coordinates with the nearest boundary pixel value. For edges near the raster perimeter, multiple samples may map to the same boundary pixel, creating repeated reads of a single value that inflates that pixel's contribution to sun_fraction. This is data fabrication — the clip should instead mask those samples as nodata and exclude them from both terms.

The sun_fraction proportion is presented as the routing input with no acknowledgment that it is a sample mean with variance p(1-p)/n. For the 5 m interval, a 50 m edge has 11 samples and a 95% CI of ±0.30 when p=0.5. The felt-minute formula amplifies this uncertainty: a sun_fraction of 0.2 vs 0.8 yields felt-minute multipliers of 1.10 vs 1.40 — a 27% routing weight difference that is within the confidence interval for many mid-length edges.

The brainstorm records only sun_fraction and sun_timestamp. A shade_run_max_m attribute (longest contiguous shade run in meters) would distinguish a thermally useful 40 m shaded arcade from a flickering 1 m / 1 m alternating pattern — both yield sun_fraction≈0.5 but have very different pedestrian comfort value. This metric is free to compute during the same pass.

source_domain: Drone-based agricultural NDVI sampling and per-parcel aggregation
success_hints: Document that the proportion estimator is unbiased for expected shade exposure but not for comfort perception
Replace np.clip with explicit out-of-bounds masking — treat boundary-overflow samples as nodata, not as boundary pixels
Add sun_sample_count and optionally sun_fraction_ci_half (half-width of 95% CI) as edge attributes
task_context: Phase 1.5 brainstorm for Solwend edge shadow sampling — fixed 5 m interval, vectorized NumPy raster lookup, NaN for no-coverage edges, sun_fraction drives felt-minute routing weight.
